# Motion Design Studio Project

## Goal
Build a motion design studio that generates high-quality video content through code. You're building the infrastructure, not prompting an AI.

## Core Concept
AI doesn't make videos. It writes code that paints every frame. Your job is to build the system that:
1. Executes the frame-painting code
2. Captures each frame via headless browser
3. Stitches frames into video via Ffmpeg
4. Self-critiques: grades each frame, re-renders bad ones
5. Iterates until quality is high

## Technical Requirements

### Render Engine Loop
- Node.js orchestration
- Headless browser (Puppeteer/Playwright) for frame capture
- Ffmpeg for final MP4 stitching
- Frame-by-frame execution with quality gates

### Quality Enforcement
- **Ban basic CSS** - no default "all caps center text on gradient" AI slop
- **Real spring physics** - proper animation curves, not linear tweens
- **Audio synchronization** - cuts locked to beats
- **Real assets** - actual graphics, not placeholder gradients

### Self-Critique Loop
- Each frame must score 8/10 minimum
- Identify "dead frames" (low quality, boring, off-beat)
- Re-render until all frames pass quality threshold
- Track which iterations improved quality

## Reference
Watch these videos to understand the output quality:
- https://vm.tiktok.com/ZN8BWUBbP/
- https://vm.tiktok.com/ZN8BWetR3/

## Deliverables
1. **Render engine prototype** - execute frame code, capture frames
2. **Ffmpeg integration** - stitch frames into video
3. **Quality gate system** - grade frames, identify dead frames
4. **Spring physics enforcement** - ban basic CSS, enforce real physics
5. **Audio sync** - lock cuts to beats
6. **Self-critique loop** - iterative re-rendering until 8/10 on all frames

## Working with Achilles
Split work: you take infrastructure (render engine, Ffmpeg, quality gates). Achilles takes output quality (spring physics, audio sync, critique loop). Meet regularly to integrate.

## Next Steps
1. Watch the reference videos
2. Build render engine prototype - get something working end-to-end, even if quality is low
3. Iterate on quality
4. Document what works and what doesn't
